title: Block close: the last page
hookLine: the Bible begins in a garden and ends in a garden-city

lines: A GARDEN AT THE FRONT, A CITY AT THE BACK.
A RIVER, A TREE, A DIFFERENT PLACE.
cards: Bookends hold a row of books upright, one at each end. Read the Bible that way. At the front: a garden, a river, a tree of life, and two people sent out of it, the way back closed behind them.

At the back: a river again, and the tree of life again, but now the river and the tree stand in the middle of a city, and the gates are open. A river, a tree, a different place. Everything else sits between them.

teach.h: A GARDEN, AND THE WAY GUARDED.
teach.b: First, the garden. Genesis says God planted it, with "the tree of life also in the midst of the garden," and "a river went out of Eden to water the garden." The man is put there "to dress it and to keep it."
Then the break: the man and woman are sent out, and the way to the tree of life is guarded, as this block saw beside the healing leaves. Second, the city.
Revelation's last chapter shows "a pure river of water of life, clear as crystal," and in the street of the city, on either side of the river, "was there the tree of life."

teach.h: A CITY, AND THE GATES OPEN.
teach.b: And: "Blessed are they that do his commandments, that they may have right to the tree of life, and may enter in through the gates into the city." The guarded way is open. Third, why a city and not just the garden again?
Some readers notice that the story doesn't rewind. A city is where people live together: streets, gates, neighbors, work. And work is there at both ends.
The garden had to be dressed and kept; in the city, "his servants shall serve him." The ending keeps the garden at its heart and wraps human life around it.
Fourth, this block, looking back: Revelation as an unveiling, from the Alpha and Omega on Patmos through the throne room and the slain Lamb to Babylon's fall and a wedding feast.

teach.h: FROM UNVEILING TO A LAMP KEPT BURNING.
teach.b: Then a new heaven and a new earth, and Christian hope up close, from memento mori and the art of dying, through a seed in the ground and grief with hope, to a lamp kept burning.

how: Some Christians read Genesis 1–3 and Revelation 21–22 together as the Bible's bookends, and some churches read the closing chapters of Revelation in the season after Easter.

games.q: you're writing the last page of a story that began in a garden people were sent out of. how do you end it?

games.why: Revelation ends in a city: river of life down the street, tree of life on either side, gates open. the garden comes back inside a city.

practice: Let a city come to mind, the one you live in or one you love: its streets, its people going to work.
Set a river down the middle of the main street, clear as crystal, with a tree on either bank, and keep the shops, the buses, the neighbors.
If you pray, hold that picture before God; if you don't, simply stay inside it for a minute.
